roles.format_summary: log lines describing email transactions or rejections

roles.evidence: documentation:Sendmail Installation and Operation Guide, logging section
roles.role: time when the event was logged, in ISO 8601 format
name of the machine where sendmail is running
name of the program logging the event, 'sendmail'
numeric process ID of the sendmail instance
unique identifier for the email message
email address from which the message was sent
size of the email message in bytes
classification or category of the message, typically 0 for regular mail
number of recipients to whom the email was sent
unique message ID header for the email, if provided
protocol used for sending the email, typically ESMTP (Extended SMTP)
name of the daemon handling the mail transaction, 'MTA-v4' for a Mail Transfer Agent version 4
host that relayed the email, either the SMTP client or an intermediate relay server
IP address of the SMTP client initiating the connection
recipient's email address, if known and the delivery was successful
total time taken to process or deliver the message, in ISO duration format
time spent waiting for a relay to respond, in ISO duration format
method used to deliver the email, typically 'local' for local delivery
priority of the message, a numeric value indicating its urgency or importance
enhanced status code describing the delivery result
delivery status of the message, typically 'Sent' for successful delivery
text describing why a recipient was refused or why an event occurred
name of the ruleset that matched during processing, if applicable

unresolved.reason: not always present in the samples

findings.message: the inner grok reads 3 of 6 texts of `log`. It must read every one: a text it misses loses the whole line. The first it misses is "Got login request with identifier: {'type': 'm.id.user', 'user': 'ghost\xa0x0\u2003198.51.100.10'}, medium: None, address: None, user: None". every capture matches; the failure is in the literal text between them A different kind of message gets its own pattern in `inner.alternatives`.
'message' appears in 6/6 samples but is neither mapped nor listed as unresolved.
